name: Vesper Peak and Sperry Peak

legs.route: Via Headlee Pass and the ridge above Vesper Lake
South side of the west ridge
legs.connect: Drop west along Vesper's ridge to the low pass between the two, scrambling the steeper bits, then pick up a trail again at the base of Sperry and climb its steep dirt and brush.

how: Both summits share the Headlee Pass approach, so climbers take one and then cross to the other instead of hiking in twice. Vesper usually comes first. The link is the hardest part of the day: the ridge loses height fast and needs hands in places, and Sperry's final slope is more steep walking than scrambling, with one exposed move that a bushy bypass avoids.
descent: Return to the pass between the peaks, then drop granite slabs and boulders to Vesper Lake and walk its edge to the trail at the east end. From there the route rejoins the approach over Headlee Pass.
logistics: One car at the Sunrise Mine trailhead. A fit party needs roughly eight hours car to car. The pass is the main hazard: early season snow, steep switchbacks and rockfall. Best once the snow is gone, mid summer into early fall.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Order, route and times from a 2017 blog report (7h48m, 12.4 km) read in full; a 2004 scramble page confirms Sperry via the S side of the W ridge and a descent via the pass between. Search snippets (not read in full) mention a bump sometimes called Wolf Peak between the two, a 2002 same-day report (10 mi, about 5,200 ft) and a club page (10 mi, 5,800 ft); no gain figures used in text. The other pages read were Vesper-only.

name: Del Campo Peak and Gothic Peak

legs.route: South face / south gully from Foggy Lake
West ridge from the Gothic–Del Campo saddle
legs.connect: Descend from Del Campo to the saddle between the two peaks, above Crater Lake, then cross glacier-polished slabs to a notch below Gothic.

duration: 1 long day, or a weekend with a camp in Gothic Basin
how: Gothic Basin serves both summits, so they pair naturally. Del Campo goes first because it is the harder and more exposed scramble (class 3, called class 4 by some). Gothic follows by slabs to a notch, a short wall step, a traverse across the steep upper west face and then easy scrambling. A few snow patches or a moat near the Gothic summit block can complicate things earlier in summer.
descent: Come down Gothic's southeast ridge to talus and slabs above Crater Lake, walk down to the lakeshore and the lower lake, and rejoin the approach trail. This avoids retracing the Del Campo scramble.
logistics: Start at Barlow Pass: about a mile of old road to Monte Cristo, then the steep trail up through the waterfall section into the basin. Reported day times run from about eight hours to just over nine. Camping at Foggy Lake splits it into two easier days. No car shuttle.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Order Del Campo then Gothic from a 2006 write-up (about 8 h, 10am start) and a 2016 report (car at 5:20 pm). Class: one report says guidebook class 3 but others say class 4 for Del Campo; kept the higher in text. Two other pages read covered Del Campo alone. Search snippets (not read in full) also describe both peaks as a standard weekend or one long day.

name: Ingalls Peak and Fortune Peak

legs.route: From the col between the north and south summits, class 3 on the final section

legs.connect: Follow the ridge toward Fortune; it is rugged enough that the line drops to about 7,200 feet before climbing to the summit.

how: From Ingalls Pass climbers leave the trail near Headlight Basin and go cross-country to the col between the two Ingalls summits, then cross to the south peak. Fortune (also called Headlight Peak) sits along the ridge and is added as a second summit. The harder North Ingalls is also paired with Fortune by camping in Headlight Basin: the north peak's south ridge is a roped rock climb with rappels, and Fortune's east slope is a snow climb the next morning.
descent: From Fortune, drop directly toward Esmeralda Basin to meet the trail near 5,200 feet and walk out, instead of returning over Ingalls Pass. After the north-peak option, rappel the route and glissade the snow below Fortune back to camp when it is in.
logistics: Esmeralda trailhead at the end of the North Fork Teanaway road. The ridge loop is roughly 9 miles with close to 3,800 feet of gain. Late summer to fall is cleanest; spring has snow on the col and slopes.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Loop from a 2015 report (South Ingalls then Fortune, 9 mi, about 3,833 ft, back near 5:30 pm); North Ingalls plus Fortune/Headlight from a 2008 two-day report camped in Headlight Basin. The north peak's easiest route is 5.3 to 5.6 depending on line (hence the class 3 south peak is the usual pick). A search snippet (not read) describes South Ingalls then Fortune then back along the ridge to Ingalls Pass; descent varies by party.

name: Cannon Mountain and Enchantment Peak

legs.route: From Prusik Pass, class 3 with a short steeper pillar near the top
legs.connect: Cross the Druid Plateau, passing the tarns above Shield Lake and Coney Lake, to Prusik Pass, then walk west to the peak.

how: Cannon's long scramble ends on a plateau that leads straight toward Prusik Pass, so the second summit costs only a modest extra distance. The Druid Plateau has little or no water; Coney Lake is the refill point. Enchantment Peak is a walk up gravel and talus to an exposed finish with easy but vertical scrambling near the tiny top.
descent: Instead of returning the way you came, go directly toward the top of Aasgard Pass, which is hard to find from the peak (several parties were cliffed out), then down to Colchuck Lake and the trail to the car. This makes the outing a loop of about 14 miles.
logistics: Starts at the Colchuck Lake trailhead area. The route passes through Enchantments permit country, so confirm the current day-use and overnight rules before going. Done from late summer to early fall; some parties finish in darkness over Aasgard.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Class and the 14-mile loop from a 2011 report (Cannon NE ridge class 3, Enchantment Peak class 3 with a 15 ft class 4 pillar); a 2018 report did the same pairing with the Aasgard descent. The 2017 page was only searched, not read. Permit rules not confirmed.

name: Pinnacle, Plummer and Denman Peaks
region: Tatoosh Range, Mount Rainier National Park

legs.route: From the saddle, a short heather scramble
legs.connect: Go back down to the saddle and climb the short walk-up on the other side.
Follow the ridge west from Plummer, dropping to the saddle before Denman and scrambling the last stretch.

how: All three rise from the same ridge above a maintained trail, so the standard day takes them in a row from the saddle. Pinnacle is the most technical, with loose rock and exposure on the summit ridge (class 4 by some counts). Plummer is an easy walk-up and Denman a light ridge scramble. Many parties continue west to Lane, which means a harder descent and loose ground, or on toward Wahpenayo, where route finding gets much worse.
descent: Retrace the ridge to the saddle and take the trail down to the road. A full traverse of the range instead exits far along the ridge and needs a car at both ends.
logistics: Start at the Pinnacle Peak trailhead near Reflection Lakes; about 1.5 miles of trail reach the 5,900-foot saddle. Early season has hard snow on the approach and below Plummer, so carry an ice axe and crampons. Summer to early fall is best; watch the afternoon thunderstorms.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Order Pinnacle, Plummer, Denman (then Lane) from the 2001 and 2014 traverse reports; the 2008 ski report links Plummer to Denman via a saddle and calls Pinnacle a class 2 gully from the Castle saddle (kept the higher class 4 from the other sources). Lane was attempted by both traverse parties; one did not summit. Thunderstorm line is from the 2008 report. Search snippets (unread) show the same grouping scheduled by outdoor clubs.

name: Mount Washington and Mount Ellinor Ridge Traverse

legs.route: Standard climbers trail to the upper basin, then the summit block by ledges

legs.connect: Cross the ridge: a knife edge, a string of small gendarmes, a loose 50-foot downclimb to the low point, then snow or rock up to the saddle and on to the summit.

how: Climbers go up Washington first, then follow the connecting ridge to Ellinor, which gives a longer day than either mountain alone. Rock on the crest is fractured basalt with scarce protection; difficulty is class 4 to low 5th in places, and rappels of 20 to 30 meters are an option. Steep snow fingers on one side give bail-out lines.
descent: Use Ellinor's summer route down, then walk or jog the road back to the Washington trailhead. Most parties do not reverse the ridge.
logistics: Start and finish at the Washington trailhead, so the road walk back replaces a shuttle. About 6 miles and 4,250 feet of gain, reported at about four hours at an easy pace. Helmet and ice axe early in the season; water is scarce later.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Direction, features and times from a 2023 report; the route database lists it as easy 5th, grade II, with poor rock and severe exposure. Higher grade kept. A search snippet says a lower traverse through the west basin is the more common way to link the two (not read in detail).

name: Mount Anderson and West Peak

legs.route: From Flypaper Pass across the Eel Glacier, north slopes to a short scramble

legs.connect: Cross the upper Eel Glacier and climb snow slopes to a saddle on the ridge, about 100 feet of class 3, then follow the crumbly crest.

duration: 3 to 4 days from the road end
how: Camp on the moraine above Anderson Glacier, climb to Flypaper Pass and the Eel Glacier, summit the East Peak, then continue across the glacier to the ridge for the West Peak, the higher of the two. The East Peak is mostly snow with a short scramble at the top. The West Peak is far harder: a sharp, crumbly ridge with notches and pinnacles, so rope and slings are needed and several parties have turned back.
descent: Return across the Eel Glacier, either over Flypaper Pass or through Echo Col next to Echo Rock, back to the camp. Then walk out down the Dosewallips valley.
logistics: The Dosewallips road has been washed out low down; parties bike the last miles to the trailhead and then hike about 10 miles to Anderson Pass. Check the current road status. Glacier gear is required. Late spring to midsummer has the best snow bridges over the pass.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Both reports read in full (2005 and 2010) summited the East Peak and attempted but did not top the West Peak; the 2005 party turned back at a notch and the 2010 party at the summit gully and a pinnacle. Search snippets (unread) say another party summited the West Peak by the northeast ridge via Echo Col. Peak heights (7,321 vs 7,365 ft) from snippets only. Road status is as of 2005 and 2010. Snow-bridge season line is unsourced: remove if unwanted. DROPPED by reviewer: no read source confirms a West Peak summit on the same trip.

name: Mount Daniel and Mount Hinman

legs.route: From Peggy's Pond, east side to the gap below the summit pyramid, then the south ridge
Via Pea Soup Lake and the saddle west of it
legs.connect: Cross the divide to Pea Soup Lake and its west end, drop to about 5,500 feet, then climb south and southwest to the top.

how: A single camp near Peggy's Pond or Venus Lake reaches both peaks. Daniel is the shorter, direct day. Hinman is less direct: cliff bands at the lake can force a climb above either end of Pea Soup Lake, and in spring parties ski over the divide between the two. Glaciers on the north side of Daniel add crevasse hazard in summer.
descent: Return to camp the way you came and walk out via Squaw Lake. In snow, the descent is skied off the east shoulder of Daniel back toward the pond.
logistics: Cathedral Rock trailhead at the end of the Cle Elum valley road, a high-clearance road. Camps at Peggy's Pond; fires are not allowed. Ice axe and light crampons; glacier gear in summer. Spring ski and late summer are both used.
notes: Checked 2026-10-30. Thin evidence: one guide page links the peaks through the Pea Soup Lake route and a 2015 ski report did both from a camp at Venus Lake outlet (packs dropped on the divide). Search snippets (unread): another guide calls the Hinman to Daniel traverse very complex, and a 2021 report lists Hinman west ridge class 2 and Daniel Lynch Glacier class 3. No class numbers used in text. Review before shipping. DROPPED by reviewer: thin evidence and a ski-trip framing; re-research before shipping.
